body:
### Description

Related PR: #2531

A stand-alone executable subcommand does not preserve the first end-of-options delimiter (`--`) when Commander dispatches to the child process.

This means an option-like operand after `--` can be reparsed by the child command as an option, rather than as a positional argument.

### Reproduction

Parent:

```js
const { Command } = require('commander');

new Command()
  .name('parent')
  .command('child', 'run child', {
    executableFile: 'child.js',
  })
  .parse();
```

Child:

```js
const { Command } = require('commander');

new Command()
  .name('parent child')
  .argument('[input]')
  .action((input) => console.log({ input }))
  .parse();
```

Run:

```
node parent.js child -- --not-an-option
```

### Expected

The child command should receive the end-of-options delimiter and treat the following value as an operand:

`{ input: '--not-an-option' }`

### Actual

The child command reports an unknown option:

`error: unknown option '--not-an-option'`

### Notes

Commander already treats the first `--` as an end-of-options delimiter for normal parsing, consistent with POSIX Utility Syntax Guideline 10[^1]. The README also documents `--` as ending option processing, with remaining arguments used without being interpreted[^2].

For stand-alone executable subcommands, the README says the executable is responsible for handling its own options, rather than declaring them at the top level[^3]. But in this case the parent consumes the delimiter before spawning the executable, so the child does not receive the same end-of-options boundary from the original command line.

I think the compatible behavior is to keep the existing in-process command behavior unchanged, but restore the first delimiter only when spawning an executable subcommand.

[^1]: https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/basedefs/V1_chap12.html#tag_12_02
[^2]: https://github.com/tj/commander.js/blob/ba6d13ddb4243e5913367734f8c159089ffe7834/Readme.md?plain=1#L200
[^3]: https://github.com/tj/commander.js/blob/ba6d13ddb4243e5913367734f8c159089ffe7834/Readme.md?plain=1#L703

comments.body: I was aware of the behaviour. Often the `--` get used when passing through options for another command, which is what is happening here behind the scenes. But ideally the implementation decision to use external subcommands would be transparent.

There have been multiple Pull Requests which all inject the end-of-options delimiter (`--`) back in later. Please don't blindly open any more Pull Requests without some consideration on whether you are offering something different than previous attempts.

I wonder whether removing the `--` from the arguments being processed could be delayed until it reaches the leaf command. This would be a subtle change to the argument processing loop and how arguments are categorised on the fly, but feels consistent with the high level intent. Stop option processing when delimiter encountered, eventually don't return the delimiter in the parsed arguments, but can postpone when the delimiter removal occurs until read the leaf command.

I am working on a change which means `--` will be passed to subcommand when mixed with subcommand arguments:
```console
node parent.js child -- --not-an-option
```

But to keep things simple will not be passed to external subcommand if occurs before subcommand, like:
```console
node parent.js -- child --not-an-option
```

title: Executable subcommand does not preserve end-of-options delimiter before option-like operands

body:
Hello, I'm opening this issue to gather feedback from the community about adding support for a plugin api and what would it look like.

If you are interested in having plugin support in commander.js, please comment and let us know your thoughts!

See below for a list of resources compiled by @shadowspawn

---
_Originally posted by @shadowspawn in https://github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2503#issuecomment-4197222405_

For interest, I have been collecting plugin links and Commander issues and have not previously posted this info. (The last item musing about approaches does match this PR approach.)

- plugins?? Future direction for expansion and customisation?
    - Commander issues
        - https://github.com/tj/commander.js/pull/907#issuecomment-505769990  
        - https://github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/1619  
        - https://github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/1197#issuecomment-653700165
        - https://github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/1292 
    - https://oclif.io/docs/plugins 
        - They can export 3 different types: commands, hooks, and other plugins.
        - hooks: init, rerun, postrun, command_not_found
    - https://github.com/infinitered/gluegun 
    - https://jmcdo29.github.io/nest-commander/docs/features/plugins/ 
    - middy: middleware
    - Cordova has lot of plugins
    - Koa has LOTS of middleware (>200?)
    - fastify: https://www.fastify.io/docs/latest/Write-Plugin/ 
    - https://yarnpkg.com/features/plugins#what-can-plugins-do
        - add resolvers, fetchers, linkers
        - add new commands
        - register to some events
    - https://github.com/getgauge/taiko/wiki/Taiko-Plugin 
    - https://github.com/unifiedjs/unified#plugin
    - plugin approach
        - plugin offers hooks and commands (say), restricts what plugin can do
        - plugin just runs code and modify command object directly. Allows say calling exitOverride, adding commands and/or options, et al
---

## Possible interfaces

### Fastify-like register api

- See implementation in https://github.com/danielpza/commander-register and https://github.com/tj/commander.js/pull/2503

```js
new Command()
  .option('-c, --compress')
  .command('sub-command')
  .register(prettyErrors)
  .register(setMeta)
  .register(logger)
  .action(() => {
    // noop
  })
  .parse();

// vs

const command = new Command() // forces binding the new command to a variable
  .option('-c, --compress')
  .command('sub-command')
  .action(() => {
    // noop
  })
  .parse();

prettyErrors(command);
setMeta(command);
logger(command);

// or worse
logger(
  setMeta(
    prettyErrors(
      new Command()
        .option('-c, --compress')
        .command('sub-command')
        .action(() => {
          // noop
        })
        .parse(),
    ),
  ),
);
```

comments.body: Created a userland implementation of the register plugin api in https://github.com/danielpza/commander-register. This should be (hopefully) temporary until a plugin api lands in commander.

I might be missing something. These two comments seem to conflict? Unless you mean it is ok for Commander to look for nearest file, but you don't want the program author to need to refer to a higher level `package.json`.

> When it's called, commander use will use the nearest `package.json` file

I had noticed possibility for looking for `package.json` for version, but good suggestion that could also get name and description too.

(I am slightly surprised Node.js does not have a nice way of returning `package.json` contents or location, since in many cases node loaded and processed `package.json` to work out what entry point to use for the package.)

> Unless you mean it is ok for Commander to look for nearest file, but you don't want the program author to need to refer to a higher level package.json.

Exactly what I mean.

> (I am slightly surprised Node.js does not have a nice way of returning package.json contents or location, since in many cases node loaded and processed package.json to work out what entry point to use for the package.)

These [api](https://nodejs.org/api/module.html#modulefindpackagejsonspecifier-base) can help.

Nice, thanks for link! Currently still experimental.
`findPackageJSON` added in https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/55412

In my experiments, the "base" for the `findPackageJSON` search seems the fragile part to finding the root `package.json`. 

Using self-contained code which uses itself as the base in a linked package will not find the root package since it is in a different part of the file system and not "above" the calling code. Likewise I think for code in workspaces.

Allowing the caller of `program.usePackageJson()` to optionally specify a suitable starting directory for the search (like in the original post) would hopefully allow caller from root code to provide correct reference base.
